title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
mechanism: Environment-policy pairs co-evolve through environment mutation, minimal-criterion admission, novelty selection, within-environment ES optimization and direct/proposal policy transfer.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/1901.01753v3#S3 : Algorithm 2 describes environment generation, paired optimization and transfer.
https://arxiv.org/html/1901.01753v3#S6 : Algorithms 3-4 detail minimal criteria, archive novelty and ES-based transfer.
Section 4.3 compares direct optimization, direct-path curriculum and no-transfer controls; no performance magnitude is reproduced in this chapter.
limitations: Section 5 acknowledges bounded environment encodings and fixed morphology.
Direct-path control matches ancestor-path ES cost, not necessarily total population-wide research cost.
No proof of unbounded complexity or self-rewriting optimizer; current repository URL not yet independently confirmed.
source_doc: User-requested primary research expansion; not a linked paper in the two original notes

title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
mechanism: Generate reasoning with current model, filter by provided correct answers, rationalize failures using answer hints, remove hints for training, and fine-tune anew from the original base each round.
evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2203.14465#S3 : Algorithm 1 and text explicitly state reset to the original pretrained model each round; current trained model generates next-round data.
limitations: Needs supplied questions, correct answers and seed reasoning examples; not supervision-free.
Correct final answers can accompany false or unfaithful rationales; Section 6 and Appendix G discuss this.
HTML mirror content was read, not claimed as a complete primary-host full-text reading; no unverified official repo asserted.
source_doc: User priority list; S3Gym/Aspire primary related-work sections supplied corroborating leads

title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
sections_read: arXiv submission history and author code link
mechanism: An existing LM expands a human-seeded task pool with instructions and input-output examples, filters invalid/near-duplicate instances, then instruction-tunes the original model on the collected corpus.
evidence: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2212.10560#S2 : classification uses output-first generation, other tasks use input-first; Section 2.3 places fine-tuning after data generation.
limitations: Task-pool feedback is not evidence that generator weights are updated every generation batch.
ROUGE filtering cannot certify semantic correctness; seed bias, long-tail coverage and API reproducibility remain issues.
No empirical percentage is reproduced without a table-bound claim; official repo link is supplied by the paper.

title: Beyond Human Data: Scaling Self-Training for Problem-Solving with Language Models
mechanism: Generate/E-step samples solutions to external training prompts and filters by binary feedback; Improve/M-step resets to the base model and fine-tunes on retained outputs before next-round resampling.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06585v4#S3 : EM interpretation, Algorithm 1 and explicit differences from original ReST.
https://arxiv.org/html/2312.06585v4#S5.SS3 : larger single-round sample pool, one-solution-per-question and reset-vs-continuation ablations.
limitations: External questions and reward remain necessary.
Exact EM monotonicity does not guarantee test improvement under finite sampling, reset and approximate optimization; APPS regressions are reported.
No author-endorsed code repository URL confirmed in inspected paper.

title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
mechanism: Instruction-following model also judges its candidate responses; self-scored preference pairs train the next model by iterative DPO. IFT/EFT seed data initialize both roles.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2401.10020v3#S2 : model/data iteration and self-reward pipeline.
Section 3.1.3: fixed Llama 2-Chat generates prompts; evolving model generates and judges responses; Claude 2 is used for validation early stopping.
Section 3.1.1: EFT justifications are model-generated and filtered for agreement with human rankings.
limitations: Self-reward does not mean all pipeline components are autonomous or no human seed exists.
Section 6 discusses response-length growth, reward hacking and correlated judge biases; limited iterations in one setting do not establish indefinitely compounding gains.
No author-endorsed code repository URL confirmed; do not substitute a third-party reimplementation without labeling it.

mechanism: R1-Zero uses GRPO directly from pretrained base with rule-based accuracy and format rewards. R1 adds cold-start SFT, reasoning RL, rejection-sampled/general SFT and later RL; released distilled models use teacher-generated SFT.

Original paper, hardened later releases and Lite differ in aggregation and invalid-run rules; do not combine rankings without protocol reconciliation.
Judge-based audit and explicit prompt rules are not robust permission enforcement or contamination proofs.

title: ParetoRSI-Gym: Can AI Agents Improve Language Models Across Multiple Domains?
sections_read: HTML v1: sections 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.4, 4.1-4.3, Limitations; appendices A-B, C, D.1-D.3, F-G
mechanism: An agent revises a multi-domain data pool and written principles using proxy traces, selects a historical checkpoint and bounded LoRA SFT settings, then evaluates final/proxy-selected checkpoints on unexposed generalization suites.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34386v1#S2.SS3 : checkpoints can restart, branch or continue; fixed training family does not mean all hyperparameters are fixed.
https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34386v1#S3.SS4 : Final, Proxy Best and Domain Best are distinct; Domain Best combines different rounds and is not one deployable checkpoint.
Section 3.2 and Appendix B preserve conversation history despite Section 2.2 describing principles as the only evidence channel.
Appendix D.3 shows that a cross-domain improvement can later be partly lost; no headline average is reproduced here.
limitations: Average improvement need not be Pareto improvement; some score gains reflect output-format learning.
Persistent-history wording and data-only shorthand are not fully consistent with detailed execution protocol; this chapter retains the distinction.
Automatic decontamination does not exclude semantic or pretrained overlap.
Moving proprietary backbones, narrow language/domain scope and unequal replication limit comparisons; no official repository URL confirmed.

title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
sections_read: Primary HTML v2: sections 2-3, 4.1-4.4, 5, Appendix B.1-B.2 and D.2
Catalog version history and abstract; author repository link supplied by the primary paper
mechanism: Completed discovery trees become prefix-observable replay worlds. A fixed agent rewrites executable exploration-policy code; candidate policies are evaluated on all archived worlds and the highest replay-scoring one is redeployed online. Online discoveries enlarge the history pool. Base models, evaluator and execution interfaces remain fixed.
persistent_state: B: archived discovery trees, snapshots, execution outcomes and replay pool
D/F boundary: executable exploration-policy versions, not neural base-model weights

sources.reading_scope: Retrieved original method and experimental passages; not certified full-paper reading or complete source-code audit.

evidence: Section 3: 'Only the policy code changes'; models, evaluator and execution interfaces stay fixed.
Section 3 replay: 'no outcome outside' the recorded tree is produced. Candidate development can use historical feedback, but the executed policy is restricted to revealed prefixes.

Section 3 Equation 1 scores normalized quality-cost hypervolume minus a sequential-rounds/calls penalty; selection includes the incumbent. Nondecrease holds on the same replay pool, not on future online outcomes.
Appendix D.2 prohibits unrevealed scores, hardcoded winning cell IDs and raw trace access inside the policy; prompt rules alone are not verified isolation.

numeric_claims.protocol: Author-reported Gemini-3.1-Pro, five rounds for Dream-RSI and Recursive Fixed Exploration; discovery uses 17 synthetic instances, final runtime measured on six held-out datasets. Mean runtime 3587.1 to 2931.0 ms, discovery calls 550 to 317. The approximately 162x SimpleTES comparison uses a different backbone.
numeric_claims.source_phrase: average improvement over fixed exploration is driven by RCV1
numeric_claims.limitation: The other five Pro evaluation datasets become slower; calls are not total compute, token cost or latency.

numeric_claims.protocol: Four representative KernelBench tasks, Gemini-3.1-Pro, L40S, nine rounds, correctness checks plus inverse-runtime scoring. VGG16/LayerNorm require 2.43x/1.79x fewer generations at comparable performance; ConvDiv/ConvMax attain 2.09x/1.44x performance at comparable discovery-call budgets.
numeric_claims.limitation: Not all KernelBench tasks; no single common speedup metric across different quality-versus-budget comparisons. Some Appendix B table budget cells are absent in text extraction, so exact numerical per-round caps are not reproduced.

numeric_claims.protocol: Terminus-Kira seed, Claude Opus 4.8 for discovery, policy development and harness execution; full 89-task Terminal-Bench 2.1, two runs/task. Author-reported score 0.7247 to 0.8090.
numeric_claims.limitation: Fixed-exploration full-search ablation was not performed for cost reasons; full-suite score participates in discovery, not an untouched confirmation set.

limitations: Replay cannot estimate unobserved branches or counterfactual agent generations; online ordering can change context and outcome distributions. These are Atlas deductions from the documented interface, not a quoted impossibility theorem.
Incumbent retention guarantees only in-pool replay nondecrease; repeated selection can overfit the simulator.
Discovery-agent calls exclude policy-development calls and do not equal full token, evaluator, GPU or wall-clock cost.
Section 5 all-history versus current-history ablation uses different realized calls, so it is not an equal-compute history-capacity intervention.
Scientific tasks include a controlled fixed-exploration baseline; expensive harness search does not. No base-model training or independent replication performed here.
